articles.title: Vì sao phi tần không thể tự ý quát mắng cung nữ?
articles.text:
Không giống như trong phim ảnh, các vị phi tần không thể tự ý quát mắng cung nữ. Lý do vì sao?
Trong các bộ phim cung đấu của Trung Quốc, chúng ta thường thấy những cảnh phi tần khi tức giận thường đánh phạt thái giám, cung nữ. Tuy nhiên trên thực tế, các học giả lại cho rằng phi tần trong hậu cung có thể đánh nhưng không thể tùy tiện mắng như vậy, nếu không họ có thể lãnh hậu quả nghiêm trọng. Tại sao vậy?
Theo "Thanh sử cảo" ghi chép, trong hậu cung thời phong kiến, cung nữ có địa vị khá thấp. Họ được đưa vào cung để hầu hạ cho các vị chủ tử. Họ không chỉ phục vụ cho mọi hoạt động sinh hoạt của các chủ tử mà đôi lúc còn phải làm những công việc bẩn thỉu, nặng nhọc. Trong nhiều cảnh phim, chúng ta thấy nhiều phi tần khi gặp chuyện không vừa ý thường trút giận lên đầu cung nữ.
Các chủ tử không thể quát mắng cung nữ trong cung. (Ảnh minh họa)
Nhưng trong lịch sử hoàn toàn ngược lại, khi triều đình nhà Thanh sụp đổ, một số cung nữ đã tiết lộ sự thật: Trong cung, các chủ tử không được quát mắng cung nữ, nguyên nhân gồm 3 điều sau:
Thứ nhất, các vị phi tần biết rằng nếu dùng những lời lẽ thô tục mắng cung nữ sẽ khiến bản thân mất đi khí chất khuê tú của bản thân. Đặc biệt khi họ tức giận sẽ khó kiềm chế bản thân, làm ra những hành động lỗ mãng ảnh hưởng đến hình tượng của người trong hoàng tộc.
Thời xưa, các bậc quân vương luôn đề cao phẩm hạnh của phi tần hơn nhan sắc. Nho giáo có câu: “Dung nhan đoan trang, mộc mạc mới thể hiện ra giá trị của khí chất. Phục sức nếu quá xa hoa thì sẽ lộ ra sự dung tục”. Có ý, phụ nữ phải con trọng chuẩn mực, lề lối, đặc biệt là trong lời ăn tiếng nói.
Thứ hai, trong cung người qua lại nhiều, khi trách mắng cung nữ một cách gay gắt khó tránh khỏi trở thành câu chuyện bị mọi người bàn tán. Trong quá trình truyền tải câu chuyện có thể sẽ bị "thêm mắm dặm muối" khiến sự việc tưởng chừng nhỏ nhặt lại bị thổi phồng quá đà. Sự việc đến tai hoàng thượng, sẽ khiến thiên tử cảm thấy vị phi tần này chua ngoa đanh đá mà ghét bỏ. Không ít phi tần vì chuyện này mà thất sủng thậm chí bị đày vào lãnh cung.
Cuối cùng, cung nữ làm việc trong cung trong thời gian dài đều nắm rất rõ sự tình. Vị phi tần nào đang tranh đấu với ai, bôi nhọ ai, ít nhiều cũng nắm giữ bí mật nào đó. Khi tùy ý đánh mắng và động thủ với họ, trong lúc tuyệt vọng có thể các cung nữ sẽ nghĩ quẩn mà tiết lộ hết bí mật của các vị phi tần, đây là điều mà họ rất e sợ.
Quy tắc đã rõ ràng như vậy nhưng nhiều phi tần vì quá tức giận đã lỡ trách phạt thậm chí động thủ với cung nữ mà dẫn đến hậu quả bị hoàng thượng ghét bỏ.

articles.title: Rejuvenation breakthrough: Scientists reverse 60 years of aging in human cells
articles.text:
Rejuvenation breakthrough: Scientists reverse 60 years of aging in human cells
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Bonn
- Summary:
- Scientists have turned blood cells from an 80-year-old into neural stem cells with a molecular age of less than 20, effectively reversing more than 60 years of cellular aging in the laboratory. The discovery offers a new way to investigate how cells become younger and could help researchers better understand age-related diseases such as Alzheimer's.
- Share:
Scientists in Germany have found a way to dramatically reverse the molecular age of human cells, transforming blood cells from an 80-year-old person into stem cells with an age signature of less than 20 years.
Researchers at the University Hospital of Bonn and the University of Bonn achieved this remarkable transformation by reprogramming immature red blood cells into neural stem cells, which can eventually develop into brain cells. During the process, molecular markers associated with aging were effectively reset, making the cells more than 60 years younger at the molecular level.
Unlike earlier approaches, the rejuvenation happened gradually, allowing scientists to follow the changes over an extended period. This slower process could provide important clues about how cellular aging can be reversed and potentially help researchers investigate treatments for diseases associated with aging.
The findings were published in the journal Aging Cell.
How Scientists Turn Blood Cells Into Brain Stem Cells
The human body contains hundreds of specialized cell types, all of which originate from a single fertilized egg and carry essentially the same genetic instructions. As cells develop, however, they take on specific roles. Under normal circumstances, a skin cell cannot transform into a liver cell, and a blood cell cannot become a nerve cell.
Modern laboratory techniques have made it possible to overcome these biological restrictions. Scientists can now reprogram certain mature cells to adopt entirely different identities. For example, skin cells can be converted into cells capable of producing nerve tissue, an approach that could eventually contribute to treatments for neurodegenerative diseases.
The process relies on a combination of proteins called transcription factors, which regulate how genes are activated. By changing which genetic instructions a cell follows, these proteins can redirect its development and give it a new cellular identity.
"Using this method, we have directly converted red blood cell precursors into neural stem cells," explains Prof. Dr. Oliver Brüstle, director of the Institute of Reconstructive Neurobiology at the University Hospital of Bonn.
Earlier experiments by the Bonn team had already demonstrated that nerve cells generated through this approach could successfully connect with existing neurons after being transplanted into the brains of mice.
Scientists Reverse More Than 60 Years of Cellular Aging
The latest investigation focused on an especially intriguing consequence of cellular reprogramming: the dramatic reversal of molecular aging.
"In our current study, however, we focused on a different phenomenon: namely, the observation that cells become significantly rejuvenated during reprogramming," emphasizes Brüstle, who is also a member of the Transdisciplinary Research Area (TRA) Life & Health at the University of Bonn.
To determine how much the cells had rejuvenated, the researchers examined their molecular clocks, particularly biological markers known as epigenetic clocks. These clocks estimate a cell's biological age by analyzing chemical modifications to DNA that tend to accumulate or change as organisms grow older.
Importantly, these modifications do not alter the DNA sequence itself. Instead, they affect how frequently certain genetic instructions are used (epigenetics). Because these patterns change predictably with age, scientists can use them to estimate how old a cell appears at the molecular level.
The results were striking. After reprogramming, cells taken from an 80-year-old individual displayed molecular age signatures corresponding to someone younger than 20. In other words, the process had reversed more than six decades of cellular aging.
"We also know that this epigenetic rejuvenation ensures that the cells actually behave like young cells," says the scientist.
A Slower Rejuvenation Process Reveals New Clues
Scientists have previously observed that reprogramming cells can reset their biological age. However, earlier demonstrations of this effect involved a more complicated process requiring two distinct stages.
First, researchers would convert an existing cell, such as a blood cell, into a pluripotent stem cell. These versatile cells have nearly unlimited developmental "career paths" because they can give rise to many different cell types throughout the body.
The pluripotent stem cell would then be guided into becoming a neural stem cell, which is more specialized and can produce cells found in the nervous system.
This conventional approach produces rejuvenation relatively quickly, making it difficult to examine all the changes taking place.
The Bonn researchers instead bypassed the pluripotent stage entirely.
"In contrast, we converted blood cells directly into neural stem cells -- that is, without first passing through the pluripotent cell stage," said Brüstle. "In our approach, rejuvenation occurred gradually and could be tracked for over 100 days."
The researchers observed a dramatic reduction in molecular age, with the study highlighting rejuvenation of approximately 60 years after 50 days. Because the process continued over a much longer period, scientists could examine the biological changes as they unfolded rather than observing only the final result.
What Cellular Rejuvenation Could Mean for Alzheimer's Research
The ability to watch cells gradually become younger could be particularly valuable for scientists trying to understand the mechanisms that control biological aging.
By studying this extended transformation, researchers can investigate which molecular pathways are involved and test whether particular substances can speed up or slow down the rejuvenation process.
"Rejuvenation that extends over such a long period of time is ideal as an experimental model: Since the epigenetic clocks are slowly reset over several weeks, we can use this model to investigate which factors and active substances accelerate or slow down the rejuvenation process."
The findings could be especially relevant to neuroscience, where aging is closely connected to the development of serious neurological conditions. Although the work does not establish a treatment capable of reversing aging in people, it offers a laboratory model for investigating how cells regain youthful characteristics.
This could eventually help scientists better understand the cellular changes associated with conditions such as Alzheimer's disease.
"After all, age is the most important risk factor for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's!"
The research involved teams from the University Hospital of Bonn, the University of Bonn, and RWTH Aachen University. Funding was provided by the EU's Horizon 2020 program, the German Research Foundation (DFG), and the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space (BMFRT).
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Bonn. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Lea Jessica Berg, Julia Franzen, Andreas Buness, Rachel Konang, Chao Sheng, Michael Peitz, Andreas Till, Wolfgang Wagner, Oliver Brüstle. Protracted Fate Acquisition and Epigenetic De‐Aging During Induced Neural Stem Cell Conversion of Human Blood Cells. Aging Cell, 2026; 25 (10) DOI: 10.1111/acel.70751

articles.title: Tại sao lại có những cái tên Biển Chết, Biển Đen, Biển Đỏ? Tưởng kiến thức căn bản nhưng không phải ai cũng biết
articles.text:
Trên thế giới có những vùng biển nổi tiếng có cái tên rất lạ như biển Đen, biển Đỏ, biển Chết. Nghe nói đến rất nhiều nhưng không phải ai cũng biết được lý do sâu xa tại sao chúng lại được gọi như vậy. Đôi khi chính vì có tên lạ, gây tò mò mà những vùng biển này trở nên nổi tiếng hơn.
Nước biển nơi đây có màu xanh lam sẫm.
Biển Đen hay Hắc Hải là một biển nội địa nằm giữa vùng Đông Nam của châu Âu và vùng Tiểu Á. Biển Đen được nối với Địa Trung Hải qua eo biển Bosporus và biển Marmara. Nó có diện tích khoảng 422.000km2, với độ sâu nơi sâu nhất có thể là 2.210m.
Cái tên Biển Đen bắt nguồn từ đâu thật ra đến nay vẫn còn gây tranh cãi. Lý do mang tính khoa học hơn cả là do màu nước biển ở đây. Dù vẫn là màu xanh lam nhưng Biển Đen có màu xanh đậm hơn bình thường. Màu sắc này là do có nhiều loài tảo màu tối sinh sống trên bề mặt nước vì nồng độ muối của biển khá thấp.
Một tranh cãi khác cho rằng cái tên này do người Hy Lạp, Lưỡng Hà đặt từ thời xa xưa. Bấy giờ, họ thường dùng màu sắc để chỉ phương hướng, ví dụ màu vàng tượng trưng cho Phương Đông, màu đỏ cho Phương Nam, màu đen cho phương Bắc và màu xanh cho phương Tây. Biển Đen nằm ở phía Bắc đất nước Hy Lạp nên được gọi như vậy.
Biển Đen cũng có thể thật sự mang ý nghĩa "đen tối". Vào thời xưa, có nhiều con tàu đã bị chìm ở đây vì thời tiết khắc nghiệt, nguy hiểm. Vì vậy mà người dân gọi là Biển Đen như một lời cảnh báo.
Có phong cảnh rất đẹp nhưng Biển Chết lại thực sự chết chóc.
Biển Chết hay còn gọi là Tử Hải thực chất không phải là biển. Về tính chất, nó vốn là hồ nước mặn nằm ở biên giới giữa Bờ Tây, Israel, Jordan, cụ thể là trên thung lũng Jordan. Hồ có diện tích 810km2 với độ sâu tối đa là 330m.
Cái tên kỳ dị và khiến người ta sợ hãi của Biển Chết thực sự bắt nguồn từ sự nguy hiểm của nó. Vì độ mặn trong nước quá cao, không có loài cá hay các thủy sinh vật lớn sống được ở đây. Những sinh vật tồn tại được ở Biển Chết là vi khuẩn và nấm mốc rất nhỏ. Những loài cá, sinh vật từ sông Jordan bơi vào biển này đều sẽ chịu chung số phận là chết rất nhanh.
Dẫu vậy, không phải 100% sinh vật sông bơi đến Biển Chết đều không thể sống sót. Vào tầm mùa đông, khi trời mưa nhiều, lượng muối ở hồ sẽ giảm xuống khoảng 30%. Lúc này, các loài tảo có thể sinh sống ở đây.
Biển đỏ đôi khi có sắc hồng vì một loài tảo biển.
Không nổi tiếng bằng Biển Đen hay Biển Chết, Biển Đỏ hay Hồng Hải là một vịnh nhỏ của Ấn Độ Dương, nằm giữa châu Phi và châu Á. Biển Đỏ thông ra đại dương ở phía nam thông qua eo biển Bab-el-Mandeb và vịnh Aden. Biển Đỏ rộng khoảng 450.000km2 và nơi sâu nhất là 2.500m.
Cũng tương tự như người anh em Biển Đen, Biển Đỏ không hề có màu đỏ thực sự nhưng có chút sắc đỏ. Nguyên nhân nước biển lẫn màu đỏ là do lượng tảo lớn có màu đỏ tên Trichodesmium erythraeum sống ngay trên bề mặt. Nhưng hiện tượng này cũng chỉ xảy ra vào một khoảng thời gian ngắn nhất định trong năm. Cũng có ý kiến cho rằng màu đỏ này đến từ các dãy núi giàu khoáng chất màu đỏ gần đó.

articles.title: Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
articles.text:
Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- Penn State
- Summary:
- A new Penn State study suggests that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults. After 12 weeks, participants showed meaningful gains in balance, leg strength, and their ability to stand up from a chair, all important factors for maintaining independence and reducing fall risk.
- Share:
A daily strength training routine lasting just four minutes can significantly improve strength, balance, and mobility in older adults, according to new research led by Penn State College of Medicine. The findings suggest that maintaining physical independence with age may require much less exercise than many people assume.
Published in the journal PLOS One, the study found that adults aged 65 and older experienced meaningful improvements in physical performance after only 12 weeks. These gains are especially important because muscle strength and mobility influence the risk of falling, the ability to live independently, and overall health and longevity.
For older adults, being able to move comfortably and perform everyday activities is essential for maintaining quality of life. Simple tasks such as standing up from a chair, climbing stairs, and walking can become more difficult as strength and balance decline.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, unintentional injuries, including those caused by falls, are among the leading causes of death in adults aged 65 and older.
Despite the importance of physical fitness, many older adults believe that meaningful improvements require long, demanding workouts. Christopher Sciamanna, professor of medicine and public health at Penn State College of Medicine and lead author of the study, says the new findings challenge that assumption. Even a brief daily routine can improve important measures of mobility and physical function.
"The human body is designed to improve very quickly," Sciamanna said. "And just a few repetitions of an exercise performed regularly can lead to huge improvements. Exercise is about forward thinking -- think about what you want to be able to do and train for it."
Why Shorter Workouts Could Make Exercise Easier
Strength training, also known as resistance training, involves making muscles work against some form of resistance, such as body weight or elastic bands. Research has shown that it can substantially improve muscle strength within a few months.
However, fewer than one in five older adults meet the recommendation to perform muscle strengthening activities at least twice a week. Common obstacles include discomfort, limited time, and the physical demands of conventional exercise programs.
Another challenge is that planning an effective workout can feel overwhelming, particularly for people who are unfamiliar with exercise.
"Exercise is actually really complicated, because you have to decide how many repetitions, how far, how many sets, how much rest, and how many times per week," said co-author Smita Dandekar, associate professor of pediatrics at Penn State College of Medicine. "It's hard work, so there's huge problems with people wanting to do exercise. If we can make it short, we're part way there."
The researchers had already seen encouraging results from an earlier experiment called FAST (Functional Activity Strength Training)-1. In that smaller study, 24 older adults performed just 30 seconds of push-ups and squats each day. After six months, their ability to perform squats had improved.
Other research has similarly suggested that performing only a few sets of exercises each week can produce strength improvements approaching those achieved with considerably longer workouts.
These findings led Sciamanna and his colleagues to investigate whether an especially brief exercise program could produce measurable improvements in older adults.
Testing a Simple Four-Minute Exercise Routine
For the new study, the Penn State researchers developed a program called FAST-2 to evaluate whether a short daily workout could improve mobility and physical ability in adults older than 65.
The trial included 97 participants whose average age was 74. They were randomly divided into two groups, with one following the exercise program and the other receiving no intervention.
Before the study began, participants reported exercising for an average of only about 18 minutes per week. That was far below the general recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity each week, Sciamanna explained.
The FAST-2 routine consisted of four simple movements:
- Push-ups: To strengthen muscles in the upper body.
- Chair stands: Repeatedly standing up from a seated position to work the legs.
- Two-arm rows: Pulling against resistance to strengthen the upper body.
- Stair stepping: Stepping up and down to challenge the legs and support functional mobility.
Each exercise lasted 30 seconds, followed by 30 seconds of rest, bringing the complete routine to four minutes.
Participants received four elastic resistance bands and an adjustable-height stepper, along with written instructions explaining how to perform each movement. The researchers also provided easier variations to accommodate different physical abilities.
For example, participants could perform push-ups against a wall or countertop rather than on the floor. Those who found chair stands challenging could use their hands on their knees for additional support.
As their strength improved, participants were encouraged to make the exercises progressively more difficult. Someone performing modified push-ups might advance to the standard movement, while another participant might increase the height of the stepper.
To evaluate the program, researchers measured how quickly and effectively participants could rise from a chair and how long they could balance on one leg. These assessments were conducted at the beginning, midpoint, and end of the 12-week study.
Such tests are valuable because they reflect movements people rely on throughout the day. Performance on these assessments can also help predict future mobility problems, fall risk, and the potential need for additional care.
Significant Strength and Balance Improvements in Just 12 Weeks
The results showed that the brief exercise program produced significant gains in physical function, even though it involved only 60 seconds of lower body resistance training per session.
Participants demonstrated several measurable improvements:
- 4.2 additional chair stands: An increase in the number of times participants could stand up from a chair within 30 seconds.
- 3.6 more seconds of balance: An improvement in how long participants could remain standing on one leg.
- 2.3 seconds faster: A reduction in the time needed to complete the sit-to-stand assessment.
These changes may seem modest, but they reflect physical abilities that are essential for everyday independence. Stronger legs and better balance can make activities such as getting out of a chair, climbing stairs, and walking easier to perform.
Sciamanna emphasized that these simple physical tests can reveal important information about a person's future health and independence.
"These indicators predict your future ability to go into a nursing home, your future likelihood of falling and of developing difficulty walking," Sciamanna said. "They give you a sense of whether or not you're going to be able to be active in the future."
Although the study measured improvements in physical performance rather than directly testing whether participants experienced fewer falls or avoided nursing home care, the findings suggest that short workouts could help preserve abilities closely tied to independent living.
A Workout Older Adults Can Actually Stick With
Beyond the improvements in strength and mobility, the researchers identified another major advantage of the four-minute routine: participants were able to follow it consistently.
Throughout the study, they completed their exercises on 81% of days.
That level of participation suggests that a short, straightforward workout may be easier to incorporate into daily life than a longer exercise program. It could also help people overcome obstacles such as limited time, discomfort, or difficulty maintaining a regular fitness routine.
For older adults who are largely inactive, even a small amount of consistent resistance training could therefore provide a practical starting point for improving physical function.
The researchers say their results reinforce the idea that exercise sessions do not need to be lengthy to produce meaningful benefits. By focusing on movements that support everyday activities, a few minutes of daily effort may help older adults maintain strength, mobility, and independence.
For Sciamanna, the ultimate purpose of exercise extends beyond simply becoming physically stronger. It is about preserving the ability to participate in life and continue doing the things that matter most.
"Exercise is the key to freedom," he said. "Freedom is the ability to be able to do what you want to do, and I would say that if you can't do what you want to do, you're not free. I approach exercise by thinking of what I want to be able to do in 20 years, and then I train to do that."
Study Authors and Research Contributors
Additional Penn State researchers involved in the study included Smita Dandekar of the Department of Pediatrics, Division of Hematology and Oncology at Penn State Health Children's Hospital; Jordan Kurth, Liza S. Rovniak, Noel Ballentine, and Natalia Pierwola-Gawin of the Department of Medicine, Division of General Internal Medicine at Penn State College of Medicine; and Yimeng Shang and Shouhao Zhou of the Department of Public Health Sciences, Division of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics at Penn State College of Medicine.
Jonathan G. Stine also contributed to the research. He is affiliated with the Department of Medicine, Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center and holds an additional appointment in the Department of Public Health Sciences at Penn State College of Medicine.
Other contributors included Matthew Silvis of the Departments of Orthopedics and Rehabilitation and Family and Community Medicine at Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center; Matthew A. Ladwig of Purdue University Northwest; David E. Conroy of the University of Michigan; Kathryn H. Schmitz of the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine; and Margaret Danilovich of Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Penn State. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Smita Dandekar, Jordan Kurth, Yimeng Shang, Jonathan G. Stine, Matthew A. Ladwig, David E. Conroy, Kathryn H. Schmitz, Liza S. Rovniak, Matthew Silvis, Margaret Danilovich, Noel Ballentine, Natalia Pierwola-Gawin, Shouhao Zhou, Christopher Sciamanna. Brief daily functional strength training to improve functional performance in older adults with mobility disability: A randomized trial. PLOS One, 2026; 21 (3): e0336748 DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0336748

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
articles.text:
NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover just shattered the all-time off-world driving record
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- NASA
- Summary:
- NASA’s Perseverance rover has shattered a historic space exploration record, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. Its advanced self-driving system helped it surpass Opportunity’s 28.06-mile record in just five and a half years, a feat that previously took nearly 15. Now, Perseverance is exploring some of the oldest rocks in the solar system, searching for clues about ancient Martian environments that may once have supported life.
- Share:
NASA's Perseverance rover has officially set a new driving record on another world, traveling farther across an extraterrestrial surface than any vehicle before it. On October 11, its odometer reached 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers), surpassing the previous record of 28.06 miles (45.16 kilometers) held by NASA's Opportunity rover, which explored Mars from 2004 to 2018.
Even more impressive is how quickly Perseverance accomplished the feat. Opportunity needed nearly 15 years to cover its record distance, while Perseverance did it in just five and a half years. The milestone came on the rover's 2,006th Martian day, known as a sol.
The record was set as Perseverance made its way toward a location called "Idubi," traveling through an area beyond the western rim of Jezero Crater known as "Lac de Charmes." This region contains what may be some of the oldest terrain ever examined in the solar system.
The landscape preserves a remarkable glimpse into the distant past. Similar rocks on Earth have largely disappeared because of erosion and the continual movement of the planet's crust through plate tectonics (Mars doesn't have tectonic plates). At Idubi, scientists hope to uncover evidence of ancient hydrothermal systems, where heated water once circulated through rocks and may have created conditions suitable for life.
How NASA's Self-Driving Mars Rover Broke the Record
One of the biggest reasons Perseverance has been able to travel so far is its sophisticated autonomous driving system.
Known as AutoNav, the technology allows the rover to navigate much of the Martian landscape without waiting for detailed driving instructions from Earth. As Perseverance moves, it continuously captures images of its surroundings, constructs a three-dimensional map of potential obstacles, and selects a safe route between destinations chosen by mission controllers.
NASA engineers describe this process as "thinking while driving."
The system operates while Perseverance travels at or near its maximum speed, allowing the rover to cover as much as 1,351 feet (412 meters) in a single Martian day.
More than 90% of the distance Perseverance has traveled has involved AutoNav evaluating the terrain. By comparison, the earliest versions of autonomous navigation used by Opportunity and its twin rover, Spirit, were responsible for assessing only about 5% of their driving distances.
The technological progress is even clearer when compared with NASA's first Mars rover, Sojourner. That early robot evaluated just 20 measurement points to determine the safest route ahead. Perseverance now analyzes approximately 600,000 points each time it examines the surrounding terrain.
"It is an honor to be working on Perseverance at a moment when the technology has evolved to the point that drives like these are routine," said Steven Lee, the project manager of the Curiosity and Perseverance rovers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "The original mission called for no more than 12.4 miles of driving. We've blown well past that, and with all mobility systems fully operational and favorable extended-ground-life test results, we expect Perseverance to keep adding to this record for many years to come."
NASA has already approved Perseverance's first mission extension. Beginning in October, the extended mission will allow the rover to continue investigating the rim of Jezero Crater through approximately the end of 2028.
Nearly 30 Years of Mars Rover Exploration
Perseverance's achievement builds on almost three decades of robotic exploration on Mars. With each new generation, NASA's rovers have become more capable of traveling longer distances, navigating difficult terrain, and investigating locations that earlier vehicles could never have reached.
The journey began in 1997 with Sojourner, a small rover roughly the size of a microwave oven. During its 83-sol mission, it traveled approximately 330 feet (100 meters).
NASA took a major step forward in 2004 with the arrival of Spirit and Opportunity. These golf-cart-size rovers were originally designed to operate for just 90 Martian days, but both dramatically exceeded expectations.
Spirit covered 4.8 miles (7.7 kilometers) before its mission ended in 2010 after it failed to survive the harsh Martian winter.
Opportunity continued operating much longer, remaining active for an extraordinary 5,111 sols. In 2015, it became the first vehicle to complete a marathon distance on another world. Its total mileage eventually established the driving record that Perseverance has now broken.
Meanwhile, NASA's Curiosity rover, which landed in Gale Crater in 2012 and continues exploring today, has traveled more than 23.65 miles (38.07 kilometers).
Perseverance Is Becoming an Even Smarter Driver
Although Perseverance has already surpassed every previous extraterrestrial driving record, NASA engineers are continuing to improve its navigation capabilities.
"The rover that broke this record did so by making its own decisions about the path. Given the autonomy to just go, Perseverance is a better driver than the one that landed, and we're not done," Mark Maimone, deputy team chief for robotic operations on Perseverance, said. "Our newest software teaches Perseverance to steer less and roll more, and to check its own position against orbital maps mid-drive. The next frontier is sunlight itself. Glare in the navigation cameras is why we park by mid-afternoon if we're driving toward the Sun, and if we can teach the rover to see past those artifacts, every rover that follows gets a longer working day."
One challenge is that bright sunlight can interfere with the rover's navigation cameras, making it harder for its software to interpret the terrain. When Perseverance travels toward the Sun, mission planners currently stop driving by mid-afternoon to avoid these problems.
Finding ways to overcome that limitation could allow Perseverance and future Mars rovers to spend more time exploring each day.
The rover's record also extends beyond Mars. Earlier in its journey, Perseverance exceeded two historic driving distances achieved on the Moon.
In 1972, Apollo 17 astronauts Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt traveled 22.2 miles (35.7 kilometers) across the lunar surface. The following year, the Soviet Union's robotic Lunokhod 2 rover covered 24.2 miles (39 kilometers). Perseverance has now surpassed both of those distances.
Exploring 4-Billion-Year-Old Rocks for Signs of Ancient Life
For NASA, however, setting mileage records is not the primary objective. The rover's ability to travel farther and faster allows scientists to investigate more geological formations, examine a greater variety of rocks, and piece together Mars' environmental history.
Perseverance has already explored several dramatically different landscapes. Its journey began on an ancient lakebed inside Jezero Crater and continued through the remains of a river system that once carried water and sediment into the basin.
Along that route, the rover encountered a rock called "Cheyava Falls," where scientists identified a potential biosignature. A biosignature is a feature or chemical pattern that could provide evidence of past life, although nonbiological processes can sometimes produce similar clues.
The rover has since climbed toward the crater rim, where scientists are investigating a different type of ancient environment. Instead of the lake and river habitats examined earlier in the mission, researchers are now interested in the possibility that hydrothermal activity once occurred in this region.
Such systems form when water interacts with hot rocks, potentially creating chemical conditions that could support microbial life.
So far, Perseverance has gathered 29 samples of rock and regolith, the loose material that covers the Martian surface. These samples come from several distinct environments, including the crater floor, a fan-shaped deposit left by an ancient river, and the crater rim.
Some rocks in the rim region formed during major impacts approximately 4 billion years ago. They preserve evidence from an extremely early period of planetary history, much of which has been lost on Earth through geological activity.
After completing its investigation of Lac de Charmes, Perseverance is expected to continue traveling along the crater rim before heading south during its extended mission.
One future destination is Rainbow Falls, an enormous piece of ancient Martian crust measuring 328 feet (100-meter-wide). The formation was pushed upward by the powerful impact that originally created Jezero Crater.
As Perseverance continues its journey, each additional mile could bring scientists closer to understanding the ancient environments of Mars and whether the Red Planet once possessed the conditions necessary for life.

articles.title: A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
articles.text:
A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- Heriot-Watt University
- Summary:
- A decades-long mystery beneath the North Sea has finally been solved. Scientists have confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was created when a 160-meter-wide asteroid struck Earth roughly 43 to 46 million years ago. The violent collision blasted a towering curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers into the air and triggered a tsunami more than 100 meters high.
- Share:
A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea roughly 43 to 46 million years ago, triggering a tsunami more than 100 meters (330 feet) high. Now, after more than two decades of scientific disagreement, researchers have uncovered compelling evidence confirming the ancient collision.
The impact created what is now known as the Silverpit Crater, a massive structure buried deep beneath the seafloor. Although scientists first discovered it in 2002, its origins remained fiercely debated, with some researchers arguing that geological processes, rather than an object from space, were responsible.
A research team led by Dr. Uisdean Nicholson of Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh has now provided the strongest evidence yet that Silverpit was formed by an asteroid or comet. By combining advanced seismic imaging, microscopic examination of rock samples, and computer simulations, the scientists have reconstructed the violent event and identified minerals that could only have formed under extraordinary pressure.
The findings, published in Nature Communications, establish Silverpit as one of the relatively few confirmed impact craters on Earth.
A Mysterious Crater Beneath the North Sea
The Silverpit Crater lies approximately 700 meters beneath the seabed in the southern North Sea, about 80 miles off the coast of Yorkshire, England. The crater itself measures roughly three kilometers across and is surrounded by a much larger, 20-kilometer-wide region of circular faults, which are fractures in the rock where movement has occurred.
When scientists first identified the formation in 2002, several features suggested that it had been created by a high-speed collision with an asteroid or comet.
Its nearly circular outline, elevated central peak, and surrounding rings of faults resembled structures found at other impact sites. Central peaks can develop when rocks compressed by a powerful collision rebound upward, somewhat like the way water rises in the center after an object splashes into a pool.
However, not everyone was convinced.
Some geologists proposed that the unusual formation resulted from the movement of underground salt deposits, which can deform the rock layers above them. Others suggested that volcanic activity had caused part of the seabed to collapse, producing a structure that only appeared to be an impact crater.
The disagreement persisted for years. In 2009, geologists even voted on the competing explanations, as documented in Geoscientist magazine. Most participants rejected the asteroid impact hypothesis.
The latest findings show that the impact explanation was correct.
Scientists Find the Smoking Gun for an Ancient Asteroid Impact
The breakthrough came from combining newly available seismic images with microscopic evidence recovered from beneath the seabed.
Seismic imaging allows geologists to investigate structures hidden underground by analyzing how sound waves travel through different layers of rock. This technique can reveal buried faults, craters, and other formations that cannot be observed directly.
Using the improved data, Nicholson and his colleagues were able to examine Silverpit's internal structure in unprecedented detail.
But the most decisive evidence came from tiny mineral crystals discovered in rock cuttings collected from an oil well near the crater.
Dr. Uisdean Nicholson, a sedimentologist in Heriot-Watt University's School of Energy, Geoscience, Infrastructure and Society, said: "New seismic imaging has given us an unprecedented look at the crater.
"Samples from an oil well in the area also revealed rare 'shocked' quartz and feldspar crystals at the same depth as the crater floor.
"We were exceptionally lucky to find these -- a real 'needle-in-a-haystack' effort. These prove the impact crater hypothesis beyond doubt, because they have a fabric that can only be created by extreme shock pressures."
Shocked minerals are particularly important because their internal crystal structures have been altered by immense pressure. Such changes can occur when an asteroid strikes at tremendous speed, generating powerful shock waves that pass through the surrounding rock.
Ordinary geological processes generally cannot produce these distinctive microscopic features. Their discovery at the same depth as the crater floor provides strong physical evidence that an extremely violent impact occurred.
A 160-Meter Asteroid Unleashed a Monster Tsunami
With the crater's origins established, researchers used numerical models, or computer simulations based on physical laws, to reconstruct what happened during the collision.
Their results suggest that an asteroid approximately 160 meters across approached from the west and struck the seabed at a shallow angle.
Although much smaller than the asteroid associated with the extinction of the dinosaurs, an object of this size could still release an enormous amount of energy when traveling at cosmic speeds.
According to the simulations, the impact violently displaced vast quantities of rock and seawater, producing a towering curtain of debris before the material collapsed back into the ocean.
Dr. Nicholson said: "Our evidence shows that a 160-meter-wide asteroid hit the seabed at a low angle from the west.
"Within minutes, it created a 1.5-kilometer-high curtain of rock and water that then collapsed into the sea, creating a tsunami over 100 meters high."
That means the collision sent material nearly a mile into the air before it fell back into the sea, generating a tsunami taller than a 30-story building.
Unlike ordinary wind-driven waves, tsunamis involve the movement of enormous volumes of water. They are typically generated when a sudden disturbance, such as an earthquake, underwater landslide, or asteroid impact, rapidly displaces the water above it.
The estimated height of Silverpit's tsunami comes from computer modeling of the ancient impact rather than direct observation. Nevertheless, the reconstruction illustrates just how destructive even a relatively modest asteroid can be when it strikes the ocean.
A Scientific Debate Finally Settled After Decades
For Professor Gareth Collins of Imperial College London, the discovery brings a satisfying conclusion to a controversy he witnessed firsthand.
Collins participated in the 2009 debate over Silverpit's origins and contributed the numerical simulations used in the new research.
Professor Collins said: "I always thought that the impact hypothesis was the simplest explanation and most consistent with the observations.
"It is very rewarding to have finally found the silver bullet. We can now get on with the exciting job of using the amazing new data to learn more about how impacts shape planets below the surface, which is really hard to do on other planets. "
The findings do more than settle an old argument. They also give scientists a valuable opportunity to study the underground damage caused by high-speed asteroid impacts.
Because much of Silverpit's structure remains buried and well preserved, researchers can investigate how the collision fractured, displaced, and reshaped the surrounding geological layers.
These observations could help scientists interpret impact structures on other worlds, where the subsurface effects of collisions are often much more difficult to examine.
Why This Rare Asteroid Crater Matters
Earth has experienced countless asteroid and comet impacts throughout its history, but relatively few recognizable craters remain.
Weathering, erosion, sediment deposition, and plate tectonics continually reshape the planet's surface. Over millions of years, these processes can wear down, bury, or completely destroy evidence of ancient collisions.
As a result, exceptionally preserved impact sites like Silverpit are scientifically valuable.
Dr. Nicholson said, "Silverpit is a rare and exceptionally preserved hypervelocity impact crater.
"These are rare because the Earth is such a dynamic planet -- plate tectonics and erosion destroy almost all traces of most of these events.
"Around 200 confirmed impact craters exist on land, and only about 33 have been identified beneath the ocean.
"We can use these findings to understand how asteroid impacts shaped our planet throughout history, as well as predict what could happen should we have an asteroid collision in future."
Hypervelocity impacts occur when objects strike at extremely high speeds, typically several kilometers per second. At those velocities, even an asteroid measuring only a few hundred meters across can deliver a devastating amount of energy.
With its origins now confirmed, Silverpit joins a small group of important underwater and buried impact structures, including the Chicxulub Crater in Mexico, associated with the mass extinction that wiped out the nonavian dinosaurs, and the Nadir Crater off the coast of West Africa, another recently confirmed asteroid impact site.
Together, these craters provide evidence of the powerful role cosmic collisions have played in shaping Earth's geological and biological history.
By studying Silverpit's remarkably preserved features, scientists hope to better understand what happens when an asteroid strikes the ocean, how the surrounding rock responds, and what such an event might mean for Earth in the future.
The research was funded by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC).

articles.title: Kinh ngạc thiên đường trên một dãy núi
articles.text:
Tại vùng đất Navajo thuộc tiểu bang Arizona, miền Tây Nam nước Mỹ, có một dãy núi mà cảnh tượng như thể trên thiên đường, đó là núi Antelope.
Kiệt tác được mẹ thiên nhiên ban tặng
Cách mà hẻm núi Antelope sinh ra cũng khiến nhiều người tò mò và hào hứng sau đến thăm quan. Theo đó, hẻm núi Antelope được hình thành do sự xói mòn của đá sa thạch, lũ quét và các quá trình tác động khác của nước mưa, gió mùa,... qua vài triệu năm trước trên vùng đất thuộc bộ tộc da đỏ lâu đời nhất ở Hoa Kỳ. Nhiều người dân nơi đây ví hẻm núi Antelope như món quà được mẹ thiên nhiên ban tặng.
Dãy núi này mở cửa từ năm 1997 để đón chào tất cả những ai muốn chiêm ngưỡng kỳ quan có một không hai trên thế giới. Dãy núi gồm những vách núi sa thạch, nằm trong khuôn viên của công viên Navajo Tribal Park.
Nơi đây được coi như một phòng trưng bày nghệ thuật ngoài trời của các vị thánh. Những đường nét "chạm khắc" siêu nhiên, không tưởng của tạo hóa làm mê hoặc bất cứ ai đã từng đặt chân đến vùng đất này. Hẻm núi Antelope được cấu tạo bởi nhiều lớp địa chất khác nhau, chủ yếu là sa thạch và đá vôi. Khi ánh sáng chiếu vào, cùng những vách đá uốn lượn đầy kỳ vĩ, tạo nên hiệu ứng ánh sáng màu cam, đỏ, tím,... mang lại hình ảnh rực rỡ và đầy mê hoặc cho hẻm núi. Chính điều này đã mang đến cho hẻm núi Antelope biệt danh "Nhà thờ ánh sáng". Bên cạnh đó, sự mềm mại của những vách đá uốn lượn còn khiến nhiều người liên tưởng đến những dải lụa trong lòng đất.
Điều đặc biệt của sa thạch nơi đây là loại đá được hình thành từ những đụn cát hóa thạch của sa mạc Jurassic rộng lớn trước đây. Tuổi của hóa thạch này được xác định niên đại vào khoảng 200 triệu năm.
Những đường nét uốn lượn kỳ diệu chính là kết quả của dòng chảy, tác động của lũ lụt và sức lùa của gió. Các đường lượn sóng có những màu sắc khác nhau được gọi là Liesegang Bands. Chúng được hình thành bởi sự chuyển động và kết tủa ôxy hóa của sắt và mangan.
Những lát cắt lồi lõm, dần theo thời gian ăn sâu vào khối đá đã tạo nên tác phẩm mà ngày nay con người xưng tụng là "tác phẩm của thần thánh". Hẻm núi diệu kỳ hẻm núi Antelope được chia làm hai phần Antelope Thượng (Upper Antelope) và Antelope Hạ (Lower Antelope). Mỗi phần mang một vẻ đẹp riêng biệt.
Antelope Thượng là phần khe núi nằm phía trên. Mỗi khi được ánh sáng soi rọi, nơi đây trở nên lung linh, huyền ảo như bức tranh cổ tích. Đặc biệt, khi mặt trời chiếu ánh nắng chói chang xuyên qua các khe núi, hẻm Antelope mới thực sự hiện nguyên vẻ đẹp kiêu sa, "lộng lẫy" của mình.
Antelope Thượng có hình như chữ A, nằm trên cao và khá bằng phẳng, nên du khách dễ dàng đi bộ để thăm quan. Nơi đây giống như một hang động không có mái che, vào cuối mùa xuân đến đầu mùa thu, những tia nắng xuyên qua toàn bộ xuống đáy hẻm núi, tạo nên một gian ánh sáng mê hoặc lòng người.
Phần còn lại của hẻm núi hay còn gọi là Antelope Hạ, có hình dáng tựa như cặp sừng của một chú linh dương đầu bò. Ngoài cái tên Antelope Hạ, vùng này được gọi là Hasdestwazi, tức là vòng cung đá uốn lượn hình xoắn ốc.
Antelope Hạ có hình chữ V và có nhiều ánh sáng hơn Antelope Thượng. Tuy nhiên, nơi đây nằm sâu trong lòng đất, có những đường hầm hẹp và dốc, thế nên nếu muốn tham quan, bạn phải xuống tương đương với 3-4 cầu thang để vào hẻm núi, đi qua một vài chiếc thang nhỏ hơn và những tảng đá.
Tuy nhiên, vùng Antelope Hạ luôn ẩn chứa nhiều hiểm họa như những cơn lũ bất ngờ. Vì vậy, muốn khám phá nơi đây đòi hỏi những du khách có tính cách ưa mạo hiểm. Nếu đặt chân được đến vùng "địa ngọc" này chắc chắn quý khách sẽ có được những bức ảnh hoàn hảo nhất vì những phản chiếu ánh sáng và cảnh đẹp nơi đây.

articles.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
articles.text:
Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- Pensoft Publishers
- Summary:
- Deep inside a high-altitude Chinese cave, scientists discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail that has evolved to live entirely in darkness, marking the first recorded discovery of its kind in China. Named after a faceless mythical creature, the rare species may already be in danger, with researchers finding only three living adults.
- Share:
A newly identified freshwater cave snail in China is offering scientists a rare glimpse into the little-known aquatic ecosystems hidden beneath East Asia. Published in the journal Subterranean Biology, the discovery represents an important step forward in understanding the region's underground wildlife. Until now, no freshwater cave snails had been documented in China, and the country's subterranean freshwater mollusks had received relatively little scientific attention.
The newly discovered species, Erhaia dijiang, has evolved remarkable features that allow it to live in complete darkness. As a true cave-dwelling animal, it has entirely lost its eyes, with the structures normally associated with vision having fully degenerated. The tiny snail also has a cone-shaped, nearly transparent shell, a delicate body without pigmentation, and long, slender tentacles.
Its unusual appearance inspired a name drawn from ancient Chinese mythology. Researchers chose dijiang in honor of "Di Jiang," a mountain patron god portrayed as a faceless beast in the ancient text Classic of Mountains and Seas (山海经). The connection is particularly fitting because the snail is extremely sensitive to light. During laboratory observations, individuals consistently retreated into dark spaces beneath rocks whenever they were exposed to illumination.
The location of the discovery is just as remarkable as the animal itself. Scientists found Erhaia dijiang at an elevation of 2,062 meters, making it the highest-altitude cave snail yet recorded within the family Erhaiidae. The finding demonstrates that freshwater cave snails can inhabit limestone cave systems at elevations above 2,000 meters.
Life in the Dark Waters of a Mountain Cave
Within its underground habitat, Erhaia dijiang lives among submerged gravel and broken rock in water less than one meter deep. The cave's water temperature stays close to 20°C, providing a relatively stable environment for the tiny mollusks.
Even when heavy seasonal rains increase the flow of water and occasionally wash a few snails out through the cave opening, they have not been observed in nearby streams. Researchers found that the animals remain confined to the cave environment, staying within two meters of its entrance.
Laboratory observations also provided clues about what these elusive creatures eat. The snails were seen feeding on diatoms, microscopic algae that grow on rock surfaces, and they also consumed fish food supplied by the researchers.
Only Three Living Snails Found, Raising Conservation Concerns
Although the discovery sheds new light on China's largely unexplored underground aquatic biodiversity, researchers are concerned about the species' future. They describe its conservation outlook as "far from optimistic."
During the first field investigation in August 2025, the team encountered an exceptionally small number of snails. Despite searching the shallow cave waters, researchers located only three living adults and one empty shell. They found no juveniles, suggesting that the known population is extremely sparse.
The scientists are now urging more comprehensive investigations of cave ecosystems throughout China to uncover additional species and better understand these fragile underground habitats. They also emphasize the need to develop conservation protections quickly for these vulnerable mollusks, which are native to highly restricted environments and could face serious threats before their populations are fully understood.

articles.title: Scientists find 10 different diets linked to slower aging
articles.text:
Scientists find 10 different diets linked to slower aging
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- DZNE - German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases
- Summary:
- A study by DZNE finds that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging—and that there is more than one way to eat healthily. The researchers examined ten dietary patterns considered healthy, including the Mediterranean, Nordic, and a plant-based diet, as well as the DASH diet, which is designed to help lower blood pressure. The findings are published in the journal Nature Communications. 
- Share:
A large study involving approximately 7,500 people suggests that eating a healthy diet may help slow biological aging, and there is no single eating plan that stands above all others. Scientists at the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) investigated 10 different dietary patterns, including the Mediterranean, Nordic, plant-based, and DASH diets. The DASH diet was specifically developed to help reduce blood pressure.
Every dietary pattern examined was associated with slower biological aging, as measured by chemical changes in DNA that reflect the body's aging process. The findings were first identified using data from DZNE's Rhineland Study and then independently confirmed in another population. The research was published in Nature Communications.
"Our study suggests that healthy eating goes hand in hand with slower biological aging. The effects are not massive, but they are measurable and relevant for prevention. By slowing the aging process, the risk of age-related diseases such as dementia or cardiovascular disorders can be reduced. Thus, healthy eating contributes to healthy aging," says Prof. Monique Breteler, Director of Population Health Sciences at DZNE and head of the Rhineland Study. "Importantly, there is probably no single 'correct' diet. According to our data, various dietary patterns are associated with slower aging, some more, some less. That is an encouraging finding, because it leaves room to tailor healthy eating to personal and cultural preferences, budget and taste."
Measuring Biological Aging Through DNA
To investigate the connection between diet and aging, the scientists analyzed dietary information and blood samples from roughly 7,500 men and women. The initial analysis included 6,470 participants in DZNE's Rhineland Study in Bonn, Germany. The researchers then tested their findings using data from another 1,034 people enrolled in the EPIC-Potsdam Study, conducted by the German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbrücke (DIfE).
Rather than relying only on participants' chronological ages, the team looked for molecular signs of aging in their blood. Specifically, they measured DNA methylation, a process involving chemical modifications to DNA that help regulate gene activity and influence how cells function.
These chemical patterns change in relatively predictable ways as people grow older, allowing scientists to estimate biological age. Unlike chronological age, which simply measures how long someone has been alive, biological age offers clues about how the body is aging at the molecular level.
"We applied three different approaches, so-called epigenetic clocks, to read biological aging from DNA methylation," explains Juliana Tavares, a doctoral researcher at DZNE and lead author of the current publication. "To this end, we leveraged state-of-the-art technology, which allowed us to cover about 850,000 sites in the DNA. This is roughly twice as many as in most previous studies."
Ten Healthy Diets Linked to Slower Aging
The next step was to determine how closely each participant followed the 10 dietary patterns. Researchers compared reported food consumption with the recommendations for each diet and assigned scores reflecting how well individuals followed those guidelines.
Because the diets emphasize different foods and nutritional goals, a person could receive a high score for one eating pattern while scoring poorly on another. In fact, participants who met one definition of healthy eating often did not meet the requirements of other diets.
"One and the same person could therefore rank high on one diet score and low on another. In other words: People who ate healthily by one standard were often not the same people who ate healthily by another. According to our data, hardly anyone counts as a healthy eater by every standard at once," says Tavares.
Despite those differences, the overall pattern was remarkably consistent. Better adherence to every one of the 10 diets was associated with slower biological aging. Some eating patterns showed stronger associations than others, but the absolute differences were relatively small.
"While there are measurable differences between the diets, they are modest in absolute terms. It's the big picture what matters," says Tavares. "In summary: When it comes to slowing down the aging process, there isn't just one healthy diet, but indeed a whole repertoire of possible diets with a positive effect."
A Surprising Finding Among Smokers
One unexpected result emerged when researchers examined the association between diet and aging among smokers. The link between healthier eating and slower biological aging was stronger in smokers than in nonsmokers, even though smokers did not generally have healthier diets.
The researchers have not yet determined what biological processes might explain this difference. One possibility is that the extensive damage caused by smoking leaves greater room for measurable improvements associated with healthier eating. However, the finding does not lessen the well-established dangers of tobacco use.
"Smoking is very harmful to health," says Tavares, "One explanation for our findings might be that there is just more health benefit to gain for smokers by eating healthy because of the enormous detrimental effects of smoking."
Different Diets Share Common Aging Pathways
The scientists also investigated which biological processes might connect the different diets to slower aging. Although each eating pattern was associated with changes at a distinct collection of DNA methylation sites, the underlying biological pathways were surprisingly similar.
More than 70% of the affected pathways were shared across all 10 diets. These processes help regulate essential functions such as cellular structure, communication between cells, and metabolism. They also play important roles in aging and the development of chronic diseases.
The researchers identified some differences that reflected the specific goals of individual diets. For example, the DASH diet was associated with pathways related to heart health, while the MIND diet, which was developed to support brain health, showed distinct associations with pathways involved in memory and cognitive function.
"More than 70 percent of the affected biological pathways were shared across all diets. These involve cell structure, cell signaling and metabolism -- processes central to aging and chronic disease. Therefore, it is understandable that the dietary patterns we examined were all linked with a slowing of biological aging," says Tavares. "A few pathways were diet-specific, and they matched each diet's main objectives: heart-related pathways were unique to the DASH diet, and pathways related to cognition and memory were unique to the so-called MIND diet, which aims to support brain health. You don't need a perfect diet -- that may be the most practical message here. But moving forward, the diet-specific pathways point to future research on targeted dietary interventions. This could be helpful in designing targeted health recommendations."

Materials provided by DZNE - German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Juliana F. Tavares, Dan Liu, Valentina Talevi, Fabian Eichelmann, Franziska Jannasch, Matthias B. Schulze, N. Ahmad Aziz, Ute Nöthlings, Monique M. B. Breteler. Associations between diet quality, epigenetic aging and epigenome in two population-based cohorts. Nature Communications, 2026; 17 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77064-4

articles.title: Phát hiện những sinh vật lạ đáng sợ tại vùng biển ở Úc
articles.text:
Các nhà khoa học mới đây đã phát hiện những loài sinh vật ma quái, đáng sợ sinh sống trong vùng biển sâu ở Úc, nơi có điều kiện môi trường khắc nghiệt.
Tháng 10/2022, một nhóm các nhà thám hiểm đến từ Viện Nghiên cứu Bảo tàng Victoria, Úc đã thực hiện một chuyến thám hiểm mang tính cách mạng tại các vùng biển sâu Ấn Độ Dương.
Loài cá thằn lằn với hàm răng dài và sắc nhọn lần đầu tiên được phát hiện trong chuyến thám hiểm vừa qua. (Ảnh: Bảo tàng Victoria).
Sau 35 ngày với tổng quãng đường di chuyển trên 11.000km, tàu nghiên cứu Investigator do Cơ quan Khoa học Quốc gia Úc điều hành đã thu hoạch được thông tin về nhiều loài sinh vật. Đặc biệt, có những mẫu loài chưa từng được biết đến trước đây.
Cuộc sống của các loài ở những vùng biển nước sâu này rất khó khăn do môi trường ở đây thiếu ánh sáng và khan hiếm con mồi, song chúng đều có thể thích nghi.
Dianne Bray, Giám đốc cấp cao Bảo tàng Victoria chia sẻ với báo chí: "Những loài sinh vật này có khả năng phát quang sinh học để thu hút con mồi, đồng thời ẩn náu hoặc ngụy trang ở độ sâu dưới đáy biển. Trong đó, có loài đã tiến hóa với cơ quan miệng to lớn, hàm răng đáng sợ".
Trong số những phát hiện mới này, có loài mà các nhà thám hiểm gọi là "Cá dơi" có thể đi dưới đáy biển với hai cái vây hình cánh tay cùng với một "mồi câu" giả đặt trong cái hốc nhỏ trên mõm để thu hút con mồi.
A: một con lươn mù với làn da trong suốt; B: Cá Nhện Tribute có vây dưới giống như cà kheo; C: Cá dơi có vây giống như bàn tay người; D: Cá thằn lằn sở hữu hàm răng sắc nhọn. (Ảnh: Bảo tàng Victoria).
Bên cạnh đó, còn có loài Cá nhện Tribute có vây dưới cực dài giống như cái cà kheo hay loài cá thằn lằn High-Winged có hàm răng dài và nhọn. Chúng đều thuộc loại cá lưỡng tính.
Đáng chú ý, loài cá thằn lằn mới này sở hữu những chiếc răng nanh khổng lồ có thể nhìn thấy ngay cả khi nó ngậm miệng hay tồn tại một cơ quan phát sáng dưới miệng, có tác dụng thu hút con mồi.
Trong khi đó, loài lươn mù (đôi mắt kém phát triển), tồn tại ở khu vực sâu khoảng cách 4km dưới mặt biển, nó có đuôi hình chữ nhật, có thể dài tới một mét nhưng chỉ nặng 50gram.
Ngoài ra, lươn mù còn mang một bộ hàm cong, luôn luôn mở và được bao phủ bởi những chiếc răng hình móc để tìm kiếm thức ăn là những loài động vật giáp xác.
Cuối cùng, các nhà khoa học còn phát hiện loài nhím biển mới, có bộ xương mỏng dẹt như bánh crepe (một loại bánh nổi tiếng của Pháp), với những chiếc gai chứa chất độc.
Theo UNESCO, năm lưu vực đại dương chính bao gồm Thái Bình Dương, Đại Tây Dương, Ấn Độ Dương, Bắc Cực và Nam Đại Dương chứa 94% động vật hoang dã và 97% tổng lượng nước trên thế giới.
Do độ sâu các vực thẳm trên biển phần lớn chưa được khám phá, khiến còn nhiều loài sinh vật lạ tồn tại mà khoa học chưa phát hiện.
Cần lưu ý rằng, những ngọn núi dưới biển này chủ yếu có nguồn gốc từ kỷ Phấn trắng Thượng - từ 65 đến 80 triệu năm trước và đây có thể là nơi sinh sống của các cộng đồng người trong quá khứ.
Môi trường sống biển của các ngọn núi dưới nước cũng dễ dàng bị hư hại bởi các hoạt động của con người, và chuyến đi này nhằm thu thập dữ liệu quan trọng cho việc bảo tồn và quản lý chúng.

articles.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
articles.text:
Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- University of British Columbia
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage. Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow. This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue.
- Share:
Statins are among the most important medications for preventing cardiovascular disease. By lowering cholesterol, they have helped save millions of lives and reduce the likelihood of heart attacks and strokes. However, these benefits can come with unwanted effects. Some patients develop muscle pain or weakness, while a small number experience serious muscle breakdown that can potentially cause kidney failure.
Scientists at the University of British Columbia (UBC), working with colleagues at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, have identified a molecular mechanism that helps explain these complications. Their findings, published in Nature Communications, could guide the development of safer statins that maintain their cholesterol-lowering benefits while minimizing muscle damage.
How Statins Trigger a Harmful Calcium Leak
To investigate what happens inside muscle cells, the researchers used cryo-electron microscopy, an advanced imaging method that allows scientists to examine protein structures in remarkable detail. Their investigation centered on the ryanodine receptor (RyR1), a protein that regulates the movement of calcium within muscle cells.
Under normal conditions, this protein functions as a controlled gateway, releasing calcium when muscles need to contract. The researchers found that statins can interfere with this process by holding the channel open. As a result, calcium escapes continuously into areas where it should be carefully regulated, creating conditions that can injure muscle tissue.
"We were able to see, almost atom by atom, how statins latch onto this channel," said lead author Dr. Steven Molinarolo, a postdoctoral researcher in UBC's department of biochemistry and molecular biology. "That leak of calcium explains why some patients experience muscle pain or, in extreme cases, life-threatening complications."
Three Statin Molecules Reveal the Mechanism Behind Muscle Damage
The researchers concentrated on atorvastatin, a commonly prescribed medication for lowering cholesterol. Although this particular drug was the main focus, their results suggest that similar interactions could occur with other medications in the statin family.
One of the most striking discoveries was the unusual way statin molecules attach to the calcium channel. Rather than acting individually, three molecules occupy a specific pocket within the protein. The first binds while the channel is closed, making it more likely to open. Two additional molecules then enter the pocket and hold the channel open, allowing calcium to continue leaking.
"This is the first time we've had a clear picture of how statins activate this channel," said Dr. Filip Van Petegem, senior author and professor at UBC's Life Sciences Institute. "It's a big step forward because it gives us a roadmap for designing statins that don't interact with muscle tissue."
This detailed understanding could give drug developers a way to address the problem at its source. By modifying the specific features of statin molecules that interfere with muscle proteins, scientists may be able to reduce unwanted effects without compromising the drugs' ability to control cholesterol.
A Potential Path Toward Safer Cholesterol Drugs
More than 200 million people worldwide use statins. Although severe muscle injury occurs in only a small percentage of patients, less serious problems such as soreness, weakness, and fatigue are considerably more widespread. These symptoms can be disruptive enough that some people discontinue their medication, potentially losing important protection against cardiovascular disease.
The discovery could eventually help researchers create treatments that are easier to tolerate, allowing more patients to continue taking medications that reduce their risk of heart attacks and strokes.
Achieving this level of understanding required exceptionally detailed imaging. Working with the high-resolution macromolecular cryo-electron microscopy facility at UBC's faculty of medicine, the team was able to observe precisely how statin molecules interact with the muscle protein. These structural insights connect a longstanding drug safety concern to a specific molecular process, providing valuable information for future medication development.
"Statins have been a cornerstone of cardiovascular care for decades," Dr. Van Petegem said. "Our goal is to make them even safer, so patients can benefit without fear of serious side effects."
Although additional research and drug development will be needed before these findings translate into new treatments, they offer a promising direction. For millions of people who depend on statins to protect their hearts, future medications with fewer muscle-related complications could make treatment more comfortable and improve everyday quality of life.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of British Columbia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Steven Molinarolo, Carmen R. Valdivia, Héctor H. Valdivia, Filip Van Petegem. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals sequential binding and activation of Ryanodine Receptors by statin triplets. Nature Communications, 2025; 16 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-66522-0

articles.title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
articles.text:
Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
- Date:
- October 20, 2026
- Source:
- Florida State University
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action. Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts and public preparedness.
- Share:
An updated hurricane forecast map is making it easier for people to identify areas threatened by storms, but new research reveals a concerning limitation. Even when people can recognize where hurricane watches are in effect, they may not feel more at risk or become more inclined to take precautions.
Researchers at Florida State University examined whether changes to the National Hurricane Center (NHC) forecast graphics improve public understanding of hurricane threats. The study involved faculty from the School of Communication within the College of Communication and Information and the Department of Geography.
The researchers evaluated an experimental graphic that expands the traditional hurricane forecast cone to include tropical storm and hurricane watches and warnings for inland areas. The familiar cone has historically placed greater emphasis on coastal regions, even though dangerous storm conditions can extend far from the shoreline.
The findings revealed mixed results. Although the revised graphic helped people without specialized weather knowledge recognize inland areas under hurricane or tropical storm watches, it did not significantly influence how dangerous they believed the storms would be or whether they intended to take protective measures. Participants also showed no improvement in identifying areas covered by storm warnings.
The updated format was developed by the NHC in 2024, and the findings were published in the American Meteorological Society journal Weather, Climate, and Society.
"The National Hurricane Center has made a number of thoughtful changes to improve how hurricane information is communicated," said Assistant Professor Elizabeth Ray, the study's lead author. "We had a simple question. Do those changes actually help people understand what the graphic is telling them about the risk they face?"
Why People Misunderstand Hurricane Forecast Maps
To investigate how the public interprets hurricane forecasts, the research team surveyed residents of Florida and Georgia. Participants were shown either the conventional hurricane cone graphic or the newer experimental version that includes additional information about inland storm threats.
People who saw the revised map were more successful at identifying locations under hurricane or tropical storm watches. However, that improvement in recognizing watch areas did not lead to greater concern about the potential danger or stronger intentions to take safety precautions.
The results also highlighted a persistent misunderstanding surrounding the familiar hurricane "cone of uncertainty." Many people incorrectly interpret the width of the cone as an indication of a storm's physical size, rather than understanding what the graphic is intended to communicate about the uncertainty in its projected track.
"For years, research has shown that people often mistake a wider cone for a bigger storm," Ray said. "Our findings suggest that even with an updated graphic, that misconception can be hard to shake."
Why Better Hurricane Warnings May Not Be Enough
The NHC introduced its expanded forecast graphic in 2024 to help people recognize that hurricane dangers are not limited to communities along the coast. Flooding, tornadoes, and destructive winds can threaten areas well inland, making it important for residents beyond coastal evacuation zones to understand their potential exposure.
By adding inland hurricane and tropical storm watches and warnings to the traditional forecast cone, the updated graphic provides a more complete picture of where dangerous conditions could develop.
However, the study suggests that adding useful information to a forecast does not automatically make people more aware of their personal risk or more likely to respond appropriately.
The researchers stressed that their findings do not call into question the quality of the NHC's weather predictions, which they consider highly accurate. Instead, the results underscore the difficulty of presenting complex meteorological information in a way that people can readily interpret and use when making safety decisions.
"Our question wasn't whether the science is good," said co-author Patrick Merle, professor and director of the School of Communication. "The science is excellent. The question is how we communicate that science so people who aren't meteorologists understand the risk they're facing.
If people find information credible but still don't understand it well enough to take protective action, then communication has fallen short. The goal is to empower people with information they can use to stay safe."
How to Better Understand Hurricane Risks
The findings point to the importance of looking beyond a single forecast image when preparing for a hurricane. Although the cone can provide valuable information about a storm's expected path, it cannot communicate every hazard that a particular community might experience.
The researchers recommend using hurricane forecast graphics alongside local weather predictions and detailed information about possible impacts. Understanding the specific threats to an area, as well as the protective steps residents should consider, can provide a more useful basis for making decisions.
"Our findings are a reminder that one graphic can only tell you part of the story," Ray said. "Don't rely on the cone alone. Pair it with clear, local information about what impacts to expect and what actions to take. That gives you a fuller picture of what the storm could mean where you live and what to do next."
The study received funding through an internal Florida State University SEED grant. The research was also informed by discussions with the NHC, which supplied the experimental forecast graphics evaluated by the team.
Bradford Johnson, an assistant professor in the Department of Geography, contributed as a co-author.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Florida State University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Elizabeth C. Ray, Patrick F. Merle, Bradford Johnson. Uncertain about the New Cone? How Nonexperts Perceive NHC’s Experimental Track-Forecast Product. Weather, Climate, and Society, 2026; 18 (3): 843 DOI: 10.1175/WCAS-D-25-0158.1
